name: Other Geotube / Sand-Container Installations on the Israeli Coast
place: Israel (Tel Aviv Hof HaTzuk, Netanya, and national cliff-protection company pilots)
year_built: no second fully-built geotube found besides Ashkelon (separate dossier); Tel Aviv Hof HaTzuk geotube planned/tendered 2019-2020, abandoned for a rock-breakwater design by 2024; Netanya TAMA 9/13 (2017) permits a geotube option, never exercised (built rock breakwaters instead, 2021-2023); 'armored geotube' pilot technology proposed Oct 2022, not deployed in the sea as of Dec 2023
closed: not applicable - no structure built to remove
type: 0 built geotube structures found beyond Ashkelon; 1 planned-then-abandoned geotube (Tel Aviv); 1 permitted-but-unbuilt geotube option (Netanya); 1 unbuilt pilot 'armored geotube' technology (SECURE Ltd, for the national cliff-protection company)

dimensions.tel_aviv_planned_geotube: 450 m long (extendable to 900 m-1 km), submerged 3 m, 250 m offshore
dimensions.netanya_scheme_built_instead: 6 of 12 planned rock breakwaters, 3.5 km beach frontage
dimensions.armored_geotube_claimed_lifespan: ~30 years vs months-to-years for plain geotextile

designer: Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality (Hof HaTzuk plan); Government Company for Protection of Mediterranean Sea Cliffs / Vaadat Lochof (Netanya TAMA 9/13 framework); SECURE LTD (armored-geotube concept)
contractor: not found (Tel Aviv geotube tender not completed/awarded before plan changed); not found for Netanya breakwaters

cost.usd_rough: NIS 11M repair ~= USD 3.3M at 2021 rates; NIS 2.45M innovation budget ~= USD 0.7M at 2022 rates

financed_by: Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality (Hof HaTzuk plan); Israeli state budget via Ministry of Environmental Protection / Government Company for Protection of Mediterranean Sea Cliffs (Netanya, armored-geotube pilot)
outcome_one_liner: No second built geotube found on the Israeli coast besides Ashkelon: Tel Aviv's Hof HaTzuk geotube was fought off by surfers (Adi Gluska, Eyal Szmulewitz) and NGOs in 2019 and by 2024 the municipality had switched to a rock-breakwater design instead; Netanya's own master plan allowed a geotube option but the company built rock breakwaters there too; a hardened 'armored geotube' pilot exists only on paper/lab trial as of the latest source
